questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What may you need to adjust to carry a passenger on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks before carrying a passenger. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: When do you not need a larger following distance?

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead of you.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions are not perfect. This means increasing distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases your motorcycle?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and approach it slowly. Then speed up and leave the dog behind. For larger animals, brake and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of proper riding clothing?
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothing protects you from injury in a collision and from weather discomfort. It provides comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: What do you NOT need to adjust when carrying a passenger?
questions.explanation: A passenger's weight causes your motorcycle to sit differently. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: How should you stop behind another vehicle?

options.text: Stop far behind the vehicle, then slowly creep up.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. The vehicle could back up without warning, or you may need space to escape from traffic behind you.

questions.question: How can you be seen better at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and ride in a position where oncoming traffic can see you easily. Keep a good space cushion so you can move if needed. Never assume another driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need compared to cars in traffic?

options.text: Much less distance to stop than cars.
Less distance to stop than cars.
As much distance to stop as cars.
More distance to stop than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: As much distance to stop as cars.
questions.explanation: In traffic, motorcycles need as much distance to stop as cars do.

questions.question: What should you do if your front tire locks while braking?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you come to a full stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again. Then re-apply the brake.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags. Do not pile loads against the back of the seat or frame. High loads raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and make it harder to balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: When riding in a traffic lane, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions
Always ride in the center of the lane
Always ride in the left part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders who wear helmets are three times more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets. This is true at any speed.

questions.question: When parking a motorcycle next to a curb, how should you position it?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it better

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
questions.explanation: Park at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: As your weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder
Should use less pressure on the front brake
Can apply the rear brake harder

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward during braking, the front wheel has more traction. This means you can press the front brake harder.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle's wind blast pushes you, you have the most room to recover if you are riding:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane
In the center portion of the lane
In the right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most space to react if wind from a passing vehicle affects your control.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should less experienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the rear of the group

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets more experienced riders watch over them from behind.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of your lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening doors, people stepping between cars, and cars pulling out.

questions.question: Which statement about close group riding is NOT true?

options.text: It takes up minimal space on the highway
The group is easy to see
The group is unlikely to be separated
The group reaches its destination faster than a spread-out group

questions.correctAnswerText: The group reaches its destination faster than a spread-out group
questions.explanation: Close group riding saves road space, is more visible to others, and keeps the group together. However, riding close does not make you arrive faster than a spread-out group.

questions.question: If your throttle becomes stuck, you should:

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times
Not try to twist the throttle

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times
questions.explanation: Try twisting the throttle back and forth to free it. If that does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older is legally intoxicated at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______.
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: In crashes between motorcycles and cars, how many are caused by the car driver failing to yield the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle-and-car crashes happen because the car driver failed to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or with your turn signals. When your left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means you are turning right or changing lanes to the right.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see farther.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see farther.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Stay flexible with your lane position at night.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.explanation: A staggered formation works well most of the time. However, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.

questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what following distance should you maintain?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are worse.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Try to get onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side near the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may make the driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily.
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Is recommended because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
Is illegal because you must ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of your lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean that way.
